A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the encapsulation of enzymes in living cells can overcome the limitations of the enzymes themselves, allowing them to perform at high rates, conversions, and elevated temperature.

we have shown that encapsulation of LsLAI into permeabilized cells of L. plantarum is a viable approach for overcoming kinetic and thermodynamic limitations of LsLai, enabling the production of tagatose at high rates and conversions.

we have shown that encapsulating L. sakei LsLAI inside of Lactobacillius plantarum that has been chemically permeabilzed allows for the production of tagatose from galactose in a batch process with high conversions, high productivity and at moderate temperatures.
The main takeaway from our work is that
encapsulation of enzymes in cells can enable reactions that are otherwise thermodynamically, kinetically, and/or stability-limted.
encapsulation of enzymes in cells that have been chemically permeabilzed can enable enzymatic processes with otherwise unfavorable kinetics, thermodynamics, and stabilities.
encapsulating enzymes in permeabilized bacteria can be an effective way to increase the productivity and stability of enzymes that are otherwise limited by kinetics and thermodynamics.
